'''Eric Zaslow''' is an American [[mathematical physics|mathematical physicist]] at [[Northwestern University]].

== Biography ==
Zaslow attended [[Harvard University]], earning his Ph.D. in physics in 1995,<ref name="cv">{{cite web|url=http://www.math.northwestern.edu/~zaslow/cv05.pdf|title=Vita}}</ref>
with thesis "Kinks, twists, and folds : exploring the geometric musculature of quantum field theory" written under the direction of [[Cumrun Vafa]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|150677}}</ref>  His research focuses on mathematical questions arising from [[Mirror symmetry (string theory)|duality symmetries]] in [[theoretical physics]] such as [[mirror symmetry (string theory)|mirror symmetry]]. With [[Andrew Strominger]] and [[Shing-Tung Yau]], he formulated the [[SYZ conjecture]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Strominger |first1=Andrew |author1-link=Andrew Strominger|last2=Yau |first2=Shing-Tung |author2-link=Shing-Tung Yau|last3=Zaslow |first3=Eric |year=1996 |title=Mirror symmetry is T-duality |journal=[[Nuclear Physics B]] |volume=479 |issue=1 |pages=243–259 |doi=10.1016/0550-3213(96)00434-8|arxiv = hep-th/9606040 |bibcode = 1996NuPhB.479..243S |s2cid=14586676 }}
</ref>

He was named to the 2021 class of fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]] "for contributions to mathematical physics and mirror symmetry".<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows_by_year.cgi?year=2021|title=2021 Class of Fellows of the AMS|publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=2020-11-02}}</ref>

Zaslow is also known for being internationally ranked in [[Ultimate (sport)|ultimate]], with seven world or national championships<ref name=cv /> and has written limericks about physics competitively.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/features/limericks/harvard.cfm |title=David Morin, Eric Zaslow, E'beth Haley, John Golden, Nathan Salwen (Harvard Team) |access-date=2015-07-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130601084926/http://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/features/limericks/harvard.cfm |archive-date=2013-06-01 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
